# sca list

[← Command reference](../commands.md)

`<sca_options>` are the [global options](../commands.md#global-options).

```text
The sca list command help

The list command is used for listing existing sca configurations and entities.
The requested entities are listed by their entity ids, separated by space
character.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] list [<list_options>] <list_entity>

list_options:

  -h, --help                    - print this help
  -o, --output-format <format>  - output format. requires a

allowed values for format are 'ids' and 'wide'.

allowed values for the list_entity are:

  - cas             - for listing existing certificate authorities
  - subcas          - for listing existing sub-ordinate certificate authorities
  - users           - for listing existing users
  - hosts           - for listing existing hosts
  - services        - for listing existing services
  - configs         - for listing existing sca configuration files
```

**Examples:**

```bash
# List all CAs
sca list cas

# List services with details
sca list -o wide services
```

**Subcommands**

- [cas](#sca-list-cas) - for listing existing certificate authorities
- [configs](#sca-list-configs) - for listing existing sca configuration files
- [hosts](#sca-list-hosts) - for listing existing hosts
- [services](#sca-list-services) - for listing existing services
- [subcas](#sca-list-subcas) - for listing existing sub-ordinate certificate authorities
- [users](#sca-list-users) - for listing existing users

## sca list cas

```text
The list certificate authorities command help

The list certificate authorities command is used for listing id's of all of the
certificate authorities defined according to the current configuration.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] list [<list_options>] cas <cas_options>

list_options:

  -h, --help                    - print this help
  -o, --output-format <format>  - output format. requires a

allowed values for format are 'ids' and 'wide'.

cas_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help
```
